MEASURED DEFECT (docs/open_items.json `spawn-in-building`): Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs placed the player's aeroplane at the DATA ORIGIN (new Vector3(0, groundY + 15, 0)), and the origin is Delisi, mid-block -- not on the avenue. Measured from the first GPU render: plane y=492.09 (terrain 477.09 + 15), bounds 490.94..495.70, and a downward ray hit collider=chunk_18 root=Buildings at y=494.64, i.e. a BUILDING SURFACE PASSED THROUGH THE AIRFRAME on frame one; scratchpad/shots/heroplane_top.png showed a roof where the plane should be. src/citymap.js:6484-6531 `_computeSpawn` has no such problem because the JS SEARCHES the real road network at load time for the nearest avenue (width >= 8 m) and snaps the spawn onto it; SpawnFinder.cs is a complete, faithful port of that search and `grep -rn SpawnFinder unity/Assets/Scripts` returned NOTHING -- its only caller anywhere was Editor/Probes/CityGeoProbe.cs. This file loads the same merged network every other runtime consumer loads (City/VegetationRenderer.cs:200-206 and City/StreetFurnitureRenderer.cs:168-174 verbatim: legacy packed lists out of city.json.gz, roadnet.json.gz merged over the top inside citymap.js:539-541's own try/catch), runs SpawnFinder over it, caches the answer for the session, and converts the GAME-frame result to the Unity transform GameLoop applies. THE YAW IS NOT JUST GeoFrame.YawToUnity, and the file carries the derivation: SpawnFinder returns `atan2(-fx,-fz)`, the Y rotation for an object whose nose is its own -Z (src/planes.js straightens every airframe to -Z), while this port's planeRoot is NOSE = +Z because Flight/PlaneModelFrame.cs absorbed that 180 degrees in `model_frame`. A naive YawToUnity therefore points the aeroplane down the road BACKWARDS -- ENE instead of WSW. yawUnity = atan2(-noseGameX, noseGameZ) = PI - yawGame, written as the two-line vector derivation so the reason survives. NEW FILE, claims 0 lines -- it ports no JS, it makes the hero's starter plane actually reach the one PlaneController the scene has. WHY NOT 35 CONTROLLERS: one aeroplane is flyable at a time and a PlaneController carries a whole flight rig (FlightModel, PlaneRaycastWorld, ground probe, ground roll, hull damage, wall contact, plane physics); 35 of those for one flown machine is the opposite of this port's perf history. The shape reused is the Enter-takes-a-parked-plane path (GameLoop.SwapToPlane -> PlaneController.Init -> PlaneModelFrame.Ensure). Order, and every step of it is load-bearing: the old `model_frame` is DETACHED before it is destroyed (Object.Destroy is deferred to end of frame and transform.Find still returns a Destroy()'d object until then, so PlaneModelFrame.Of would have handed Attach a corpse) -- and one detach takes the cockpit kit, the hinged hood and the measured box shell with it, because PlaneCockpitBaker builds all three under the measure frame; PlanePropellers is DestroyImmediate'd, since it caches blade transforms inside the model that just went and its `_built` flag is private with no reset, and PlaneController.Init's own `GetComponent<PlanePropellers>() == null` test runs in the same frame (a jet must not inherit the Mustang's blur disc); Attach, not Ensure, applies def.Scale and src/planes.js:834's orientation fix for the NEW airframe; PlaneCockpitBaker.Bake re-measures the cockpit/shell for it (the same call Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs makes, flyable:true); PlaneDamageRecord is rederived by Flight/PlaneHallFill.cs:341-356's own formulae (planes.js:1574/1575/1587 off the identity-measured box, +max.z for the nose since this frame's nose is +Z, Planes.PlaneStamina from target.js:69); and PlaneController.ReInit rebuilds the flight rig from the new row. The gun pod is deliberately LEFT -- it hangs on the flight root, not the model, and Combat/GunPod's muzzleLocal is a constant. Asset resolution is AssetDatabase, Editor-only, the established convention for every model in this port (PlaneHallFill loads all 35 the same way); in a player build or on a missing asset the hero keeps the baked machine rather than flying an invisible one.

Invisible today (opaque bg0, the rig at y=-5000, a 100 m far plane), but this project has a measured memory that a light appearing or disappearing recompiles material variants -- that was the shooting/crash freeze (docs/QUALITY_BAR.md 'Perf wave 2026-10'). URP has no per-light culling mask, and Rendering Layers would mean flipping the pipeline asset's own toggle for the whole game; what works instead is the frame order: URP raises RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering BEFORE it culls for that camera, so a light enabled there is in that camera's visible-light set and in no other's. Both lights therefore live DISABLED, with shadows off, and are switched on only while the preview camera itself renders -- which keeps main.js:296/299's measured 2.4 / 1.2 intensities and the cyan holo rim exactly as ported rather than trading the look away. The hook is removed in Stop() (unconditionally, before its `_running` early-out: ShellUi disposes the rig whether or not the preview ever started, and a subscription outliving its camera is the CharacterView.Unbind bug) and re-added in Start(). MEASURED: PREVIEWLIGHTS dirEnabled=1 before the menu, 1 with the shell built, 1 on the personage screen, 1 reopened and 1 after logout -- i.e. the scene's own sun and nothing else, through two full open/close cycles; materials 1510 -> 1510 across the open and 1554 -> 1554 across the close (the 1510 -> 1554 step is the hero body and the re-skinned airframe entering the world, not the menu); and preview_sun/preview_rim read enabled=false intensity=2.40/1.20 shadows=None with PREVIEW_RIG_HOOKED=true on the screen the preview actually runs on.
